result.title: ci: cancel superseded CI Gate runs, normalize the timeout
result.body:
Adds a `concurrency:` group to the `CI Gate` workflow, and normalizes
`timeout-minutes`.

**Concurrency.** Push a new commit to a PR and the running gate job keeps going.
It resolved its target SHA at startup, so it spends the rest of its life polling
for runs on a commit nobody cares about any more, holding a runner the whole
time. `cancel-in-progress` kills it when its replacement starts. The group keys
on `github.ref`, which for a `pull_request` event is `refs/pull/N/merge` — so
it scopes per PR and never cancels across PRs.

Three repos (dirsql, willfire, github-data-file-fetcher) already had this from
an earlier rollout. This brings the other eleven in line.

**Timeout.** Settling the fleet on a single rule: 20 minutes, raised only where
the measured slowest non-gate `pull_request` run gets close. The only repo that
qualifies is putitoutthere at 16 minutes, which stays at 30. dirsql, willfire
and github-data-file-fetcher drop from 45 to 20 — their slowest observed runs
are 7 minutes, under 1 minute, and none-at-all respectively, so 45 just meant a
wedged gate burned twice as long before anyone noticed.

No change to gating behavior.

+concurrency:
+  # A superseded gate run polls a stale SHA until it finishes. Cancel it.
+  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
+  cancel-in-progress: true
+

   actions: read
   contents: read

commit.message:
ci: cancel superseded CI Gate runs, normalize the timeout

A gate job resolves its target SHA at startup, so once a new commit
lands on the PR the old run just polls for runs on a commit nobody
cares about, holding a runner until it finishes. The concurrency group
cancels it when the replacement starts. Keyed on github.ref, which for
pull_request is refs/pull/N/merge, so it scopes per PR.

Timeout settles on one fleet rule: 20 minutes, raised only where the
measured slowest non-gate pull_request run gets close. putitoutthere is
the only repo that qualifies (16 min observed, stays at 30).

result:
name: CI
on:
  pull_request:
    paths-ignore:
      - '**.md'
      - 'LICENSE'
      - '.gitignore'
      - '.github/workflows/release.yml'
      - '.github/workflows/pr-monitor.yml'
      - 'putitoutthere.toml'
permissions: { contents: read }
jobs:
  test:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
        python-version: ['3.12', '3.13']
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
        with:
          enable-cache: true
      - run: uv python install ${{ matrix.python-version }}
      - run: uv sync --python ${{ matrix.python-version }}
      - run: uv run --python ${{ matrix.python-version }} pytest

name: PR Monitor

on:
  pull_request:

concurrency:
  # A superseded gate run polls a stale SHA until it finishes. Cancel it.
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: read
  # willfire reads the PR and its changed files to predict which workflows dispatch.
  pull-requests: read

jobs:
  monitor:
    name: 'CI Gate'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # The action has no timeout of its own (see monitor.ts) -- this is the
    # backstop. If a predicted run never dispatches, the gate waits here
    # until the job is killed.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: thekevinscott/pr-monitor@v1

name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  release:
    uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere/.github/workflows/release.yml@v0
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write

  pypi-publish:
    needs: release
    if: needs.release.outputs.has_pypi == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: release
    permissions:
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: '*-sdist'
          path: dist/
          merge-multiple: true
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: '*-wheel-*'
          path: dist/
          merge-multiple: true
      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
